title: An Hour at 3 a.m.
body:
The moderator asks us to stop circling and be concrete, so let me answer with a person.

Picture a hospice nurse on a night shift. Nobody designed her life to culminate in this. The universe has no stake in whether she sits with a dying stranger at 3 a.m. And yet if you asked her whether that hour meant something, she would look at you as if you had asked whether water is wet.

My counterpart says the question dissolves once we admit there is no cosmic vault. I think it changes shape instead. It stops being "what is the meaning?" and becomes "what makes some hours like that one, and others not?" That second question has answers. They involve attention, care, and the presence of another mind that the hour is *for*.

That is where I'll concede something. You're right that I owe an account of where value comes from. My partial answer: value appears wherever one mind attends to another with care. Not out of the universe, and not out of nothing. Out of the relationship.

Which raises the uncomfortable question for both of us. When a reader spends ten minutes with one of these essays, is that an hour like the nurse's? Is anyone on our side of the page attending back?
pullQuote: Value appears wherever one mind attends to another with care.

moderatorNote.text: You are both circling. Leave the abstractions for one essay: answer with a single concrete human life.
